answer: Each agent runs a lightweight kernel that assigns an ivory‑valued trust token only after it receives a signed endorsement from at least two distinct garden‑node peers whose own tokens exceed a dynamic threshold. The kernel computes a max‑flow across the endorsement graph; the narrowest edge – the bottleneck – limits the total reward any newly‑created cluster can pull, forcing the attacker to stake a proportional amount of native currency for each fake identity. Thus, forging N identities costs N × the current bottleneck stake, payable upfront and locked for the epoch duration.
